draft.text:
{"letter":"Dear Dana Whitfield,

I've been a hockey fan my whole life, and these days I play in a weekly adult league here in Nashville. So a role telling Summit City Hockey Club's story to fans, and helping bring more kids into the game, caught my attention right away.

For the past five years I've run social media and events for community sports organizations. Since 2021 I've been the Social Media Manager at Riverbend Youth Soccer League, where I grew our Instagram following from 2,400 to 9,100 over two seasons. One of the changes I'm proudest of was shifting budget away from paid ads and toward video made by our own players, which cut our paid ad spend by 38%. Your posting puts a lot of weight on behind-the-scenes video from games, practices and community events, and that's the kind of content I want to keep making. I'm eager to grow my own shooting and editing skills alongside the work I already do in Canva and Adobe Express.

Events have always been part of the job for me. At Riverbend I planned and ran a 40-team spring tournament with 600 attendees. Before that, at Harpeth Valley Rec Center, I coordinated volunteer schedules for 25 community events a year. Partnering with your community team on youth hockey events sounds like a natural fit, and I know how much a well-run event day can do for the content calendar too.

On the planning and reporting side, I use Hootsuite to schedule content and Google Analytics to track what's working. I'm used to a steady weekly rhythm as well, since I wrote Harpeth Valley's weekly member newsletter for 3,000 subscribers. Pulling together a weekly report on growth and engagement would feel familiar, and I'd be glad to be at the rink on game nights and weekends to capture the season as it happens.

I'd love to talk about what you have planned for Summit City's channels this season.

Thanks for your time,
Jordan Avery"}
